title: Sessions and tokens survive a process restart
asA: operator whose deploy should not sign every operator out
iWant: outstanding sessions and unconsumed sign-in tokens to remain valid across a restart of the authenticating service
soThat: a deploy is invisible to the signed-in operator and a magic link that was minted just before a restart still works

acceptanceCriteria.description: A session issued before a process restart continues to authenticate requests after the process starts back up, without a fresh sign-in and without a change of handle value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a session S is issued and then the authenticating process is stopped and started
acceptanceCriteria.when: a subsequent authenticated request is made using S's handle after the restart
acceptanceCriteria.then: the server authenticates the request, exposes the same principal id on the request context, and does not require a fresh sign-in

acceptanceCriteria.description: An unconsumed sign-in token minted before a process restart can be consumed after the restart, within its original expiry window.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a token T is minted and then the authenticating process is stopped and started, all within T's expiry window
acceptanceCriteria.when: GET /login/verify is called with T after the restart
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is a 302 to the configured post-sign-in route and carries a Set-Cookie header issuing a fresh session handle

acceptanceCriteria.description: The idle-expiry clock for a session survives a process restart; the wall-clock elapsed during the restart counts against the idle window.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a session S with idle window I is issued, then the process is stopped for a duration D and restarted
acceptanceCriteria.when: a subsequent request is made using S's handle after the restart
acceptanceCriteria.then: the server applies the same idle-expiry rule it would have applied with no restart, using the last-seen timestamp recorded before the stop
